explanation: Following Queen Victoria's death in 1901, Viceroy Lord Curzon proposed the creation of a grand memorial. It was designed by Sir William Emerson in the Indo-Saracenic revivalist style, heavily utilizing Makrana marble (the same marble used for the Taj Mahal).

text: 82. The 'Gateway of India' is an iconic arch monument in Mumbai built to commemorate the 1911 royal visit of King George V and Queen Mary. Which architect designed this structure in the Indo-Saracenic style?
explanation: The Scottish architect George Wittet designed the Gateway of India. He combined elements of the Roman triumphal arch with 16th-century Gujarati Islamic architecture. (Note: F.W. Stevens designed the nearby Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus).

text: 83. The grand layout of New Delhi, including the monumental structures of the Rashtrapati Bhavan (Viceroy's House) and the circular Parliament House (Sansad Bhavan), was primarily designed by which two British architects?
explanation: Sir Edwin Lutyens and Sir Herbert Baker were the principal architects responsible for planning New Delhi and designing its core administrative buildings in the early 20th century, creating a unique blend of classical European and Indian architectural styles.

text: 84. The 'Chand Baori' is visually one of the most striking and dramatic architectural landmarks in India, featuring 3,500 narrow, perfectly symmetrical steps descending 13 stories. What type of structure is this, and where is it located?

options.text: A royal bath in Hampi, Karnataka

explanation: Chand Baori (built by King Chanda of the Nikumbh dynasty in the 8th/9th century) is one of the oldest and deepest stepwells (vav/baori) in the world, located in Abhaneri near Jaipur. It was designed to conserve water in the arid desert region.

text: 85. The 'Meenakshi Amman Temple', famous for its enormously tall and vibrantly colored Gopurams (gateways) covered with thousands of mythological figures, is a pinnacle of South Indian architecture. On the banks of which river is it located?
explanation: The Meenakshi Temple is located in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, on the southern bank of the Vaigai River. While its roots trace back to the ancient Pandyan empire, its current magnificent form was largely built by the Nayak rulers in the 16th and 17th centuries.

text: 86. The 'Kamakhya Temple' is one of the oldest and most revered Shakti Peethas in India, featuring a unique 'Nilachal' type of architecture with a hemispherical dome over a cruciform base. In which state is it located?
explanation: The Kamakhya Temple is situated on the Nilachal Hill in Guwahati, Assam. It is a major center for Tantric practices and hosts the famous Ambubachi Mela annually.

text: 87. The 'Jagannath Temple' at Puri is a sacred Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Jagannath, famous for its annual Rath Yatra. Which king of the Eastern Ganga dynasty initiated its construction?
explanation: King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva of the Eastern Ganga dynasty initiated the construction of the massive Jagannath Temple at Puri in the 12th century. European sailors referred to it as the 'White Pagoda', in contrast to the 'Black Pagoda' (Konark Sun Temple).

text: 88. The 'Ajanta Caves' are a UNESCO World Heritage site consisting of 29 rock-cut cave monuments. What is the exclusive religious theme of the art and architecture found at Ajanta?

options.text: A mix of Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism

explanation: Unlike the nearby Ellora Caves (which feature a mix of Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain caves), the Ajanta Caves are exclusively dedicated to Buddhism. They are heavily celebrated for their masterpiece fresco paintings (like the Padmapani), largely patronized by the Vakataka dynasty.

text: 89. The 'Ellora Caves' comprise 34 monasteries and temples carved side by side into the wall of a high basalt cliff. Which dynasty is primarily credited with the patronage and construction of the Hindu caves here?
explanation: The Rashtrakuta dynasty (particularly King Krishna I) is primarily credited with commissioning the spectacular Hindu rock-cut caves at Ellora, most notably the colossal monolithic Kailasa Temple (Cave 16).

text: 90. The 'Shalimar Bagh' is a masterpiece of Mughal garden architecture, utilizing the Persian Charbagh layout adapted to a terraced, mountainous landscape. Which Mughal Emperor built it?
explanation: Emperor Jahangir built the magnificent Shalimar Bagh in Srinagar, Kashmir, in 1619, specifically to please his beloved wife, Empress Nur Jahan.

text: 91. The 'Vittala Temple' complex is the most extravagant architectural showpiece of the Vijayanagara Empire, famously known for its iconic stone chariot and 'musical pillars'. In which city are its ruins located?
explanation: The Vittala Temple is the undisputed highlight of the Hampi ruins (the former capital of the Vijayanagara Empire). Built primarily during the reign of King Devaraya II and expanded by Krishnadevaraya, its pillars literally produce musical notes when struck.

text: 92. The 'Harmandir Sahib', universally known as the Golden Temple, is the preeminent spiritual site of Sikhism. Who originally laid the foundation stone of this architecturally unique temple in Amritsar?
explanation: While the 5th Sikh Guru, Guru Arjan Dev, designed the temple, he uniquely invited a prominent Muslim Sufi saint of the Qadiri order, Mian Mir of Lahore, to lay its foundation stone in 1589, symbolizing the temple's openness to all faiths.

text: 93. The monumental 'Gommateshwara Statue' is a 57-foot tall monolithic carving of Bahubali, standing completely bare. Which ancient official commissioned this engineering marvel?
explanation: The Gommateshwara statue in Shravanabelagola, Karnataka, was commissioned by Chavundaraya, an acclaimed commander and minister of the Western Ganga dynasty, around 983 CE. It is deeply revered in Jainism.

text: 94. The 'Martand Sun Temple' is a massive, ruined Hindu temple constructed in a brilliant synthesis of Gandharan, Gupta, and Chinese architectural forms. In which state/union territory are its ruins located?
explanation: The Martand Sun Temple is located near Anantnag in the Kashmir Valley. It was built by the powerful King Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkota Dynasty in the 8th century CE, long before the Sun Temples at Konark and Modhera.

text: 95. 'Pietra dura' (parchin kari) was a highly intricate architectural decoration technique introduced to India during the Mughal era. What does this technique specifically involve?

options.text: The use of overlapping, intersecting true arches.
The inlay of highly polished, colored semi-precious stones cut to fit into white marble to create floral or geometric images.
The creation of a double-layered dome to provide external height and internal proportion.
The carving of an entire structural temple from a single downward rock excavation.

explanation: Pietra dura is the precise, intricate inlay work of semi-precious stones (like lapis lazuli, onyx, and jade) into marble. It was first extensively used in India in the Tomb of Itmad-ud-Daulah, reaching its absolute aesthetic peak in the walls of the Taj Mahal.

text: 96. The 'Bagh Caves', a group of nine rock-cut monuments containing exquisite mural paintings, were built contemporaneously with the Ajanta caves. Which ancient empire is credited with their creation?
explanation: The Bagh Caves, located in the Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh, were excavated during the Gupta Empire (around the 5th–6th centuries CE). Like Ajanta, they are celebrated for their highly refined ancient Buddhist mural paintings.

text: 97. Which of the following UNESCO World Heritage sites is a magnificent operational railway station designed by the British architect F.W. Stevens in the Victorian Gothic Revival style?
explanation: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (formerly Victoria Terminus) in Mumbai was designed by Frederick William Stevens. It is a premier example of Victorian Gothic Revival architecture in India, blended with themes deriving from Indian traditional architecture.
